title: “Can a swarm of AI fruit flies learn to trade? I’m trying to find out.” 🪰
author: Successful-Mix-5896
selftext:
I’m experimenting with a pretty unusual project:  
I’m building a swarm of autonomous AI “fruit flies” 🪰 that trade using real-time market data. Each agent makes its own decisions, gets rewarded or penalized based on performance, learns from its trades and adapts over time.  
I’m now exploring Robinhood Chain and want to integrate JEV as well.  
The system is already running in paper trading, but I’m still figuring out the best architecture — especially what should happen on-chain vs. off-chain.  
I’m not looking for investments, tokens or wallet services. I’m genuinely looking for technical feedback from people experienced with AI agents, algorithmic trading or blockchain infrastructure.  
Would love to hear how you’d approach this.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: rewarding each fly on how much it made over a short window mostly selects the lucky ones, and the swarm drifts toward whatever the last two weeks looked like. I'd reward on whether the fill and the exit happened the way the fly planned, and only score the money part over a stretch long enough to hold a hundred trades.

replies.author: Successful-Mix-5896
replies.body:
That actually makes a lot of sense. Right now dopamine/reward is tied pretty closely to trade outcomes, so I may be selecting lucky flies without realizing it.  
Separating execution/plan quality from P&L and only judging profitability after 100 trades sounds really interesting. I’m going to test this. Thanks!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: one practical thing when you try it: a hundred trades per fly gets slow fast, so score plan quality every generation and only run the money check on the flies that survive a few rounds.
